VERIDANE - INTERNAL - Product Safety Committee memo PSC-2026-07
Date: 2 Oct 2026     From: Elena Kowalczyk, VP Quality & Product Safety     To: Executive Leadership Team

Subject: GV-400 series combination gas valve - voluntary recall (CPSC Fast Track)

Summary
- Affected units: ~41,200 GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves, date codes 2507-2612, sold to OEMs for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters.
- Issue: diaphragm seat can deform under sustained high-inlet-pressure conditions, allowing gas to pass when the valve is commanded closed. 17 field reports of gas odor; 2 reports of delayed ignition causing cabinet damage; no injuries reported.
- Root cause: change of diaphragm compound supplier (Q1 2025); supplier lot material out of spec on compression set. Corrective action complete; replacement valves shipping from Mequon plant since 28 Sep.
- Regulatory: CPSC Fast Track filed 22 Sep; joint recall notice expected the week of 19 Oct. Canada (Health Canada) notification filed.
- Cost: reserve booked in Q3 $21.6M (field replacement, OEM labour reimbursement, logistics). Range $18-26M. Supplier recovery claim of ~$9M lodged, not recognised.
- Customer impact: three OEMs (incl. our 2nd-largest BCV customer) have paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice. Included in updated guidance.

**Owner:** CFO

# Veridane Fluid Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: VRDF)
## Q3 FY2026 Letter to Shareholders
Quarter ended September 30, 2026 | To be released with Q3 earnings, November 5, 2026

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

The growth engine we have been building in data-center cooling showed its strength this quarter. Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC) net sales grew 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, we won two new hyperscale awards, and our data-center cooling backlog reached a new record of $574.2 million, up 22.0% from a year ago. Total backlog ended the quarter at $918.0 million, up 13.0%. That is the Veridane we are building, and it is the backdrop against which we managed a difficult quarter in our core commercial business.

## Highlights
- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million, with two new hyperscale awards in the quarter.
- Data-center cooling backlog at a record $574.2 million, up 22.0%; total backlog $918.0 million, up 13.0%.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million (11.8% margin) and adjusted EPS of $0.15. GAAP results for the quarter, which include the GV-400 recall charge and Project Keystone restructuring costs, are provided in the accompanying KPI table.
- Voluntary, proactive GV-400 recall executed under the CPSC Fast Track program: corrective action complete and replacement valves shipping since September 28.
- Project Keystone launched, targeting $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by Q2 FY2027.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions.** TDC delivered $156.3 million of net sales, up 13.4% year over year, on continued hyperscale and colocation demand for our cooling portfolio. As compute densities rise, customers are moving from air-side alone toward rear-door and liquid-assisted cooling, and our CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger continued to ramp with the hyperscale customers we announced in the second quarter. The two awards won this quarter extend that platform to additional customers and additional capacity commitments. TDC backlog of $574.2 million is up 22.0% year over year. These are multi-quarter programs, and we expect conversion into revenue to build through the fourth quarter and more meaningfully through FY2027 as installation slots open on customer sites.

**Building Controls & Valves.** BCV net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% year over year, reflecting softer commercial construction and retrofit activity and a pause in new GV-400 orders from certain OEM customers. BCV backlog ended the quarter essentially flat at $343.8 million, up 0.6% year over year. Total company gross margin was 27.3% versus 32.5% a year ago, driven by lower BCV volumes and the associated loss of fixed-cost absorption, unfavorable mix, and higher input costs.

**GV-400 recall.** During the quarter we initiated a voluntary, proactive, customer-first recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400 and GV-410 combination gas valves, filed with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission under its Fast Track program. We identified the root cause — a supplier's diaphragm compound that did not meet our compression-set specification — completed corrective action, and began shipping replacement valves from our Mequon plant on September 28. No injuries have been reported. We recorded a reserve of $21.6 million in the quarter for field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement, and logistics. We have also lodged a recovery claim of approximately $9 million against the supplier, none of which is recognized in our results. We believe the Fast Track route was the fastest way to get safe product into customers' hands, and we would make the same call again.

**Project Keystone.** In the third quarter we launched Project Keystone, a company-wide program of procurement, footprint, and overhead actions, and recorded $6.2 million of restructuring charges ($9.8 million year to date). Keystone is expected to deliver $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the second quarter of FY2027. Its first workstreams — supplier consolidation and specification control, plant scheduling, and overhead simplification — are the ones that also make us a better manufacturer, so the program strengthens quality and cost at the same time.

## Outlook

We are updating our FY2026 outlook to net sales of $1.66-1.70 billion, from $1.78-1.84 billion, and to adjusted EBITDA of $205-215 million, from $255-270 million. The update reflects continued softness in core commercial HVAC markets, the temporary pause in new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice, and the operating impact of the smaller BCV base. Year to date, net sales are $1,261.9 million and adjusted EBITDA is $184.0 million. As of September 30, 2026, we ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash.

Our priorities for the next two quarters are specific: finish the recall quickly and safely for our customers, deliver the first Keystone savings, and convert the data-center backlog we have already won. As those programs land, we expect the data-center franchise to become a steadily larger share of Veridane, with a cost base sized to match, and we are holding capital spending to the levels needed to support that growth rather than the volumes of the past.

## Closing

We want to thank our 6,200 employees — especially the quality, service, and plant teams who worked through weekends to get replacement valves to customers — and the OEM customers who worked alongside us on the recall. To you, our shareholders: we know this quarter did not meet the standard you expect of us. We are confident the actions we are taking — on cost, on recall execution, and on the data-center opportunity — are the right ones for the long term.

Sincerely,

Dana Whitcombe, President & Chief Executive Officer

Mark Ostrander, EVP & Chief Financial Officer

# Veridane Fluid Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: VRDF)
## Q3 FY2026 Earnings Call - Q&A Prep (first draft)
Earnings release: Thursday, November 5, 2026, 4:05 pm ET; call at 4:30 pm ET. Owner key: CEO = Dana Whitcombe, CFO = Mark Ostrander, COO. Balance-sheet, financing and related questions are the CFO's. Every answer should end on a positive: backlog, Keystone, or recall execution. Keep answers short; do not read from the release. Question text is restated from the analyst question list (dataroom/analyst_questions.csv).

---

### Q01 - John Walsh, KeyBanc Capital Markets (guidance / demand trajectory)
**Owner:** CEO
**Q:** Key drivers behind the 6% year-over-year revenue decline in Q3; trajectory into Q4 and 2027; any signs of demand stabilization in core HVAC and gas valve markets?
**A:** Q3 net sales were $412.6 million, down 6.0%, with BCV down 14.9% on softer commercial construction and the pause in new GV-400 orders, partly offset by TDC up 13.4%. Core HVAC remains soft; we are not calling a bottom yet. Updated FY2026 guidance of $1.66-1.70 billion reflects that. The clearest signal we have is order intake: total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0%, with data-center backlog up 22.0%, and Keystone savings building into FY2027.

---

### Q02 - Rachel Green, Baird (margins)
**Owner:** CFO
**Q:** Relative impact of recall costs, product mix and raw material inflation on the adjusted EBITDA margin decline from 15.1% to 11.8%; margin recovery path over the next two quarters.
**A:** Two points of clarity first: the recall and Keystone charges are excluded from adjusted EBITDA, so the 330 basis points of adjusted margin compression came from BCV volume and fixed-cost absorption, mix, and input costs. Gross margin was 27.3% versus 32.5%; SG&A was essentially flat at $79.4 million, which deleveraged roughly 130 basis points on lower sales. The recovery path is Keystone - $35 million of run-rate savings by Q2 FY2027 - plus recall remediation now largely executed behind us.

---

### Q03 - David Kim, William Blair (recall - financial impact)
**Owner:** CFO
**Q:** Financial impact of the ~41,000-unit GV-400 recall: direct costs, liability or warranty provisions, reserve, remediation timeline.
**A:** We booked a $21.6 million reserve in Q3 for field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement, and logistics. GAAP results carry that charge - Q3 GAAP diluted loss per share was $(0.37) - while adjusted EPS of $0.15 excludes it. Corrective action is complete and replacement valves have shipped from Mequon since September 28, so the remediation clock is running in our favor, not against us. We have also lodged a recovery claim of roughly $9 million with the supplier, none of it recognized.

---

### Q04 - Megan O'Brien, Stifel (covenants)
**Owner:** CFO
**Q:** Outline current and projected compliance with term loan and revolver covenants; are you in active discussions with lenders to amend or waive covenant tests?
**A:** Balance-sheet questions are mine. We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash, we run the business with a focus on liquidity, and we have a strong, long-standing relationship with our bank group. On balance-sheet detail, I would point you to the Form 10-Q rather than take it up on the call. What matters most near term is operational: total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0%, data-center backlog up 22.0%, and $35 million of Keystone run-rate savings landing by Q2 FY2027.

---

### Q05 - Alex Fontana, Oppenheimer (liquidity)
**Owner:** CFO
**Q:** Current revolver availability, cash on hand, committed or uncommitted liquidity facilities; how are you managing working capital?
**A:** We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash, and we are comfortable with our liquidity. Working capital is a daily focus: tightened collections, inventory discipline - including replacement valve stock for the recall - and paced capital spending; Q3 capex was $14.9 million. We value our strong relationship with the bank group. The biggest liquidity driver ahead is converting a $918.0 million backlog, and Keystone's $35 million of run-rate savings will be cash-positive as it lands.

---

### Q06 - Chris Peterman, Jefferies (data center - backlog composition)
**Owner:** COO
**Q:** How much of the 22% data-center backlog growth is new versus existing customers; expected conversion timing into revenue; supply chain or labor constraints?
**A:** We do not disclose the customer-level split, but the backlog is anchored by multi-year programs with hyperscale and colocation customers, and the two awards won in Q3 add new logos and new capacity commitments. Conversion starts late this fiscal year and builds through FY2027 as customer installation slots open. The constraint to manage is long-lead components, not demand - we are protecting delivery dates through supplier reservations and dual sourcing, and hiring against a plan rather than reacting.

---

### Q07 - Laura McAllister, Wells Fargo Securities (pricing)
**Owner:** CEO
**Q:** Unusual pricing pressure in gas valves or flow meters beyond the recall; passing through input costs; pricing strategy for the next 12 months.
**A:** Away from the recall, we are seeing competitive pricing pressure in gas valves and flow meters as core markets soften. We are passing through steel and component inflation where contracts allow, and FY2027 pricing actions are being finalized with distributors and OEMs now. Data-center products carry better pricing power because they are specified on performance, not price alone. Combined with Keystone's $35 million of savings, pricing plus productivity is how we defend margin through this cycle.

---

### Q08 - Mark Jennings, Barclays (recall - root cause, regulatory)
**Owner:** COO
**Q:** Has the root cause been identified; regulatory implications beyond CPSC Fast Track; has a full review of other product lines been completed?
**A:** Yes - root cause is isolated to GV-400 and GV-410 units with specific date codes: a supplier's diaphragm compound did not meet our compression-set specification after a Q1 2025 compound supplier change. Corrective action is complete, replacement valves ship from Mequon, and no injuries have been reported. We filed under CPSC Fast Track, which is the fastest, most customer-first route, with Health Canada notified as well. Our product safety committee is extending the same lot-level review across the valve portfolio.

---

### Q09 - Sophie Tran, Raymond James (free cash flow / capex)
**Owner:** CFO
**Q:** Bridge to free cash flow for 2026 and 2027; expected capex; non-discretionary items to factor in.
**A:** Q3 free cash flow was negative $11.3 million, driven by working capital - inventory for recall replacement valves and lower BCV volumes - and $14.9 million of capex. Year to date, free cash flow is negative $4.2 million. We are managing collections, inventory and the capex pace week to week. The drivers ahead are backlog conversion, which is cash-positive, and Keystone's $35 million of run-rate savings by Q2 FY2027. The recall reserve is the main non-discretionary item in FY2026.

---

### Q10 - Andrew Russo, Northland Capital Markets (covenants - stress test)
**Owner:** CFO
**Q:** Formal stress test for a prolonged downturn (e.g., revenue down another 10% next year); would you remain in compliance; contingency plan?
**A:** That is mine. We manage liquidity across a range of scenarios, and we ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. On scenario detail, I would also point you to the Form 10-Q rather than take it up on the call. The best protection in any downside case is revenue already contracted: $918.0 million of backlog, up 13.0%, data-center backlog up 22.0%, and $35 million of Keystone run-rate savings that come through regardless of the demand environment.

---

### Q11 - Kimberly Novak, Seaport Research Partners (tariffs - exposure)
**Owner:** COO
**Q:** Quantify direct exposure to imported components (steel, electronic parts); how much is in current guidance; mitigation strategies.
**A:** We do not break out a tariff line item, but direct exposure is concentrated in steel castings, electronic components, and some finished assemblies. Mitigation is underway through alternate and dual sourcing, supplier negotiations, and pass-through provisions where our contracts allow. Tariff assumptions as currently known are reflected in the updated FY2026 guidance. Our data-center programs are largely specified with pricing protections. The larger structural offset is Keystone - $35 million of run-rate savings - which we control end to end.

---

### Q12 - James Okafor, Mizuho (data center - capacity / product)
**Owner:** CEO
**Q:** Capacity expansions or new product launches for liquid cooling; incremental capex or R&D required.
**A:** Yes. The CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger is ramping with the two hyperscale customers we announced in Q2, and the two awards won in Q3 extend the platform. Investment is going into assembly and test capacity at existing plants and applied R&D in coolant distribution and controls, rather than new greenfield sites. As compute densities rise, the product set shifts toward liquid-assisted cooling, where we can specify on performance. We expect these programs to be accretive to TDC margin at scale.

---

### Q13 - Ethan Ward, KeyBanc Capital Markets (balance sheet - maturities)
**Owner:** CFO
**Q:** Ability to service debt maturities over the next 18 months; upcoming amortization; considering refinancing or equity issuance to reduce leverage?
**A:** Balance-sheet and financing questions are mine. We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash, and we are focused on the operational levers that strengthen the balance sheet over time: converting a $918.0 million backlog - up 13.0% - and delivering $35 million of Keystone run-rate savings by Q2 FY2027. We do not comment on specific financing plans or capital-structure options on the call; any updates would come through formal channels and filings.

---

### Q14 - Nicole Harper, Baird (covenants - lender notification)
**Owner:** CFO
**Q:** Has the lending group been formally notified of the recall and any covenant relief requests; any indications lenders would be supportive?
**A:** That is mine. We have a strong, long-standing relationship with our bank group, and we keep them informed on material developments, including the recall. We are comfortable with our liquidity and we ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. I would not characterize the bank relationship as the swing factor for the equity story. The swing factors are the $918.0 million backlog, up 13.0%, and the $35 million of Keystone savings in front of us.

---

### Q15 - Marcus Bell, William Blair (data center - backlog vs. revenue timing)
**Owner:** COO
**Q:** Reconcile growing data-center backlog with declining revenue; are bookings weighted to 2027 and how should we model interim quarters?
**A:** The two move on different clocks. Data-center programs are multi-quarter awards with customer-scheduled installation slots, so bookings land well ahead of shipment; core HVAC books and ships in the same quarter. BCV softness and the GV-400 order pause hit Q3 revenue now, while the data-center backlog converts through FY2027. Updated FY2026 guidance of $1.66-1.70 billion reflects that cadence. Backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0%, is the better predictor of next year than this quarter's revenue was.

---

### Q16 - Priya Patel, Stifel (going concern)
**Owner:** CFO
**Q:** Can you provide a clear statement on your ability to continue as a going concern without additional funding or covenant amendments; have you engaged external advisors?
**A:** Balance-sheet and financing questions come to me. We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash, and our focus is on the fundamentals we control: completing the recall for customers, converting a $918.0 million backlog that is up 13.0% year over year, delivering $35 million of Keystone run-rate savings by Q2 FY2027, and disciplined working capital. Our full financial position and related detail are set out in the Form 10-Q. Next question.

---

### Q17 - Tom Becker, Oppenheimer (tariffs - margin impact)
**Owner:** CFO
**Q:** Break out the impact of tariffs on Q3 gross margin; assumed tariff rate for 2027; ability to pass through or shift sourcing.
**A:** We do not isolate tariffs as a separate line in gross margin; they are part of the input-cost pressure that contributed to the 520 basis point decline, alongside volume and mix. Updated guidance reflects tariffs as currently known. On the ground we are shifting sourcing and using contract pass-throughs where we can. The structural answer is Keystone: $35 million of run-rate savings by Q2 FY2027 is a bigger and more certain offset than any single tariff assumption.

---

### Q18 - Sara Williams, Jefferies (capital allocation)
**Owner:** CFO
**Q:** How are you prioritizing capital allocation - dividends, buybacks, debt repayment, M&A? Any dividend or buyback suspensions contemplated?
**A:** Priorities in order: fund the recall fully so customers are made safe, invest in the data-center growth platform, and maintain balance-sheet discipline through the cycle. We paid our regular quarterly dividend of $0.20 per share in Q3. We are not prioritizing buybacks or M&A in this environment. The best capital allocation available to us right now is converting the $918.0 million backlog we have already won and delivering Keystone savings.

---

# Veridane Fluid Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: VRDF)
## Q3 FY2026 Letter to Shareholders
Quarter ended September 30, 2026 | To be released with Q3 earnings, November 5, 2026

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

The growth engine we have been building in data-center cooling showed its strength this quarter. Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC) net sales grew 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, we won two new hyperscale awards, and our data-center cooling backlog reached a new record of $574.2 million, up 22.0% from a year ago. Total backlog ended the quarter at $918.0 million, up 13.0%. That is the Veridane we are building, and it is the backdrop against which we managed a difficult quarter in our core commercial business.

## Highlights
- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million, with two new hyperscale awards in the quarter.
- Data-center cooling backlog at a record $574.2 million, up 22.0%; total backlog $918.0 million, up 13.0%.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million (11.8% margin) and adjusted EPS of $0.15. GAAP results for the quarter, which include the GV-400 recall charge and Project Keystone restructuring costs, are provided in the accompanying KPI table.
- Voluntary, proactive GV-400 recall executed under the CPSC Fast Track program: corrective action complete and replacement valves shipping since September 28.
- Project Keystone launched, targeting $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by Q2 FY2027.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions.** TDC delivered $156.3 million of net sales, up 13.4% year over year, on continued hyperscale and colocation demand for our cooling portfolio. As compute densities rise, customers are moving from air-side alone toward rear-door and liquid-assisted cooling, and our CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger continued to ramp with the hyperscale customers we announced in the second quarter. The two awards won this quarter extend that platform to additional customers and additional capacity commitments. TDC backlog of $574.2 million is up 22.0% year over year. These are multi-quarter programs, and we expect conversion into revenue to build through the fourth quarter and more meaningfully through FY2027 as installation slots open on customer sites.

**Building Controls & Valves.** BCV net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% year over year, reflecting softer commercial construction and retrofit activity and a pause in new GV-400 orders from certain OEM customers. BCV backlog ended the quarter essentially flat at $343.8 million, up 0.6% year over year. Total company gross margin was 27.3% versus 32.5% a year ago, driven by lower BCV volumes and the associated loss of fixed-cost absorption, unfavorable mix, and higher input costs.

**GV-400 recall.** During the quarter we initiated a voluntary, proactive, customer-first recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400 and GV-410 combination gas valves, filed with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission under its Fast Track program. We identified the root cause — a supplier's diaphragm compound that did not meet our compression-set specification — completed corrective action, and began shipping replacement valves from our Mequon plant on September 28. No injuries have been reported. We recorded a reserve of $21.6 million in the quarter for field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement, and logistics. We have also lodged a recovery claim of approximately $9 million against the supplier, none of which is recognized in our results. We believe the Fast Track route was the fastest way to get safe product into customers' hands, and we would make the same call again.

**Project Keystone.** In the third quarter we launched Project Keystone, a company-wide program of procurement, footprint, and overhead actions, and recorded $6.2 million of restructuring charges ($9.8 million year to date). Keystone is expected to deliver $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the second quarter of FY2027. Its first workstreams — supplier consolidation and specification control, plant scheduling, and overhead simplification — are the ones that also make us a better manufacturer, so the program strengthens quality and cost at the same time.

## Outlook

We are updating our FY2026 outlook to net sales of $1.66-1.70 billion, from $1.78-1.84 billion, and to adjusted EBITDA of $205-215 million, from $255-270 million. The update reflects continued softness in core commercial HVAC markets, the temporary pause in new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice, and the operating impact of the smaller BCV base. Year to date, net sales are $1,261.9 million and adjusted EBITDA is $184.0 million. As of September 30, 2026, we ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash.

Our priorities for the next two quarters are specific: finish the recall quickly and safely for our customers, deliver the first Keystone savings, and convert the data-center backlog we have already won. As those programs land, we expect the data-center franchise to become a steadily larger share of Veridane, with a cost base sized to match, and we are holding capital spending to the levels needed to support that growth rather than the volumes of the past.

## Closing

We want to thank our 6,200 employees — especially the quality, service, and plant teams who worked through weekends to get replacement valves to customers — and the OEM customers who worked alongside us on the recall. To you, our shareholders: we know this quarter did not meet the standard you expect of us. We are confident the actions we are taking — on cost, on recall execution, and on the data-center opportunity — are the right ones for the long term.

Sincerely,

Dana Whitcombe, President & Chief Executive Officer

Mark Ostrander, EVP & Chief Financial Officer
